about.description:
The header-only half of Apiary: <apiary/Annotations.hpp>, whose
APIARY_* macros mark C++ declarations for Apiary's codegen, and the
CMake package that provides it as the apiary::annotations target.
A library annotated for Apiary needs only this, at build and run time;
generating bindings needs the apiary package, which depends on it.
about.summary: The APIARY_* binding annotations, as a CMake package with no Clang/LLVM dependency

build.script:
cmake -S . -B build-annotations -G Ninja ${CMAKE_ARGS} \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DAPIARY_BUILD_TOOL=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="${PREFIX}"
cmake --install build-annotations --component ApiaryAnnotations

script: python -c "import json, sys; f = json.load(open('probe.json'))['functions'][0]; print(f['name'], '->', f['return_type']); sys.exit(f['return_type'] != 'size_t')"

raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  version: "1.3.1"
  # LLVM/Clang major apiary's libTooling code is built against. apiary is a leaf
  # *tool* - consumers run it, they do not link its LLVM - so it may pin its own
  # toolchain independent of the rest of an environment.
  llvm_major: "23"

recipe:
  name: apiary-split
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/Einsums/Apiary/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 3edcd792091825280127e886774b808dfa84d2d2ec08d56b51dbff1976fe9918

build:
  number: 0

# Apiary installs as two CMake components, and each output installs one:
#   apiary-annotations - ApiaryAnnotations: the APIARY_* header, the
#                        apiary::annotations target and the package config.
#                        No Clang/LLVM, so a library that only annotates its
#                        declarations (and everything that links it) can
#                        depend on this alone.
#   apiary             - ApiaryTool: the codegen executable, the apiary_*
#                        CMake helpers and their scripts, on top of
#                        apiary-annotations.
# The components share no file, so neither output clobbers the other.
#
# apiary-annotations is not noarch: a noarch: generic package installs its
# files at the paths they were built at, and on Windows they belong under
# Library\ rather than the env root.
outputs:
  - package:
      name: apiary-annotations
    build:
      script:
        # The annotations need no LLVM, so this configures without the tool.
        # CMake still wants a C++ compiler for project(), which is all the
        # compiler below is for.
        - if: unix
          then: |
            cmake -S . -B build-annotations -G Ninja ${CMAKE_ARGS} \
              -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
              -DAPIARY_BUILD_TOOL=OFF \
              -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="${PREFIX}"
            cmake --install build-annotations --component ApiaryAnnotations
        - if: win
          then: |
            cmake -S . -B build-annotations -G Ninja ^
              -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ^
              -DAPIARY_BUILD_TOOL=OFF ^
              -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="%LIBRARY_PREFIX%"
            if errorlevel 1 exit 1
            cmake --install build-annotations --component ApiaryAnnotations
            if errorlevel 1 exit 1
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - cmake >=3.20
        - ninja
      # Nothing here is compiled, so nothing the compiler or the C stdlib
      # would add at run time belongs in the package.
      ignore_run_exports:
        from_package:
          - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
          - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    tests:
      - package_contents:
          include:
            - apiary/Annotations.hpp
          files:
            - if: unix
              then:
                - lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryConfig.cmake
                - lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryConfigVersion.cmake
                - lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryTargets.cmake
              else:
                - Library/lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryConfig.cmake
                - Library/lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryConfigVersion.cmake
                - Library/lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryTargets.cmake
      # find_package(Apiary) finds the annotations and, with the tool not
      # installed, nothing of it.
      - files:
          recipe:
            - find-package/
        requirements:
          run:
            - cmake >=3.20
            - ninja
        script:
          - if: unix
            then: cmake -S find-package -B find-package-build -G Ninja -DEXPECT_TOOL=OFF -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="${CONDA_PREFIX}"
            else: cmake -S find-package -B find-package-build -G Ninja -DEXPECT_TOOL=OFF -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="%CONDA_PREFIX%\Library"
    about:
      summary: The APIARY_* binding annotations, as a CMake package with no Clang/LLVM dependency
      description: |
        The header-only half of Apiary: <apiary/Annotations.hpp>, whose
        APIARY_* macros mark C++ declarations for Apiary's codegen, and the
        CMake package that provides it as the apiary::annotations target.
        A library annotated for Apiary needs only this, at build and run time;
        generating bindings needs the apiary package, which depends on it.

  - package:
      name: apiary
    build:
      script:
        - if: unix
          then: |
            cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja ${CMAKE_ARGS} \
              -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
              -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="${PREFIX}" \
              -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="${PREFIX}"
            cmake --build build
            cmake --install build --component ApiaryTool
        # clang-cl, not cl and not clang++: conda-forge's win-64 clangdev ships
        # static libs built against the MSVC ABI, so clang-cl links them while
        # keeping the clang frontend apiary's libTooling code needs. A GNU-driver
        # clang++ targets the MinGW ABI and would fail to link the same libs.
        #
        # compiler('cxx') is still vs2022 here, and that is deliberate: it puts the
        # MSVC STL, import libs, and Windows SDK on INCLUDE/LIB, which clang-cl
        # consumes. The clang drivers themselves ship separately on win-64 (the
        # clang/clangxx packages in build:).
        #
        # Windows conda packages land under %PREFIX%\Library, so that - not the env
        # root - is both the install prefix and where find_package(Clang/LLVM
        # CONFIG) has to look.
        - if: win
          then: |
            cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja ^
              -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ^
              -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-cl ^
              -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang-cl ^
              -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="%LIBRARY_PREFIX%" ^
              -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="%LIBRARY_PREFIX%"
            if errorlevel 1 exit 1
            cmake --build build
            if errorlevel 1 exit 1
            cmake --install build --component ApiaryTool
            if errorlevel 1 exit 1
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - cmake >=3.20
        - ninja
        # The clang drivers (clang-cl) ship apart from the clangdev libraries on
        # win-64; on unix the cxx compiler above already is clang.
        - if: win
          then:
            - clang ${{ llvm_major }}.*
            - clangxx ${{ llvm_major }}.*
      host:
        # find_package(Clang/LLVM CONFIG) + the libTooling static libs.
        - llvmdev ${{ llvm_major }}.*
        - clangdev ${{ llvm_major }}.*
        # apiary's binary directly links libz/libzstd (compression support pulled in
        # by the static LLVM libs); their run_exports carry them into run.
        - zlib
        - zstd
      run:
        # ApiaryConfig.cmake, ApiaryTargets.cmake and the header. ApiaryConfig
        # loads this output's ApiaryTool.cmake, so the two must be the same build.
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('apiary-annotations', exact=True) }}
        # apiary dynamically links the shared libLLVM (@rpath/libLLVM.<major>.dylib),
        # which lives in the major-suffixed package libllvm<major>. llvmdev's
        # transitive run_export does not cover it, so depend on it explicitly.
        - libllvm${{ llvm_major }}
        # libclang needs Clang's builtin headers (stddef.h, stdarg.h, the
        # intrinsics) at its own version, and looks for them next to the apiary
        # binary, in lib/clang/<major> (Library\lib\clang\<major> on Windows).
        # clang-<major> installs them there.
        # Without it, parsing works only when something else in the environment
        # brings matching headers; with GCC as the build compiler nothing does.
        - clang-${{ llvm_major }}
        # The bundled doc/stub render scripts (share/apiary/scripts/*.py) are invoked
        # by the apiary_* CMake helpers at a consumer's build time.
        - python
    tests:
      - package_contents:
          bin:
            - apiary
          # bin/include are mapped to Library/ on Windows for us; plain file globs
          # are not, so they are spelled out per platform.
          files:
            - if: unix
              then:
                - lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryTool.cmake
                - lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryToolTargets.cmake
                - lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryHelpers.cmake
                - lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryRun.cmake
                - share/apiary/scripts/apiary_render_cpp_rst.py
              else:
                - Library/lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryTool.cmake
                - Library/lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryToolTargets.cmake
                - Library/lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryHelpers.cmake
                - Library/lib/cmake/Apiary/ApiaryRun.cmake
                - Library/share/apiary/scripts/apiary_render_cpp_rst.py
      - script:
          - apiary --help
      # Parse a header that needs <stddef.h> with -nostdlibinc, which drops the
      # system include paths (an SDK, MSVC, glibc) but keeps the builtin headers,
      # so it can only resolve through the headers above. Without them, Clang
      # recovers by reading size_t as int and apiary still exits 0, so check the
      # type, not the exit status or the function's presence.
      - files:
          recipe:
            - probe.hpp
        script:
          - apiary --emit-cpp-docs-json --module probe probe.hpp -- -std=c++17 -nostdlibinc > probe.json
          - if: win
            then: if errorlevel 1 exit 1
          - python -c "import json, sys; f = json.load(open('probe.json'))['functions'][0]; print(f['name'], '->', f['return_type']); sys.exit(f['return_type'] != 'size_t')"
          - if: win
            then: if errorlevel 1 exit 1
      # find_package(Apiary COMPONENTS tool) finds the executable and the
      # helpers, with the annotations from apiary-annotations.
      - files:
          recipe:
            - find-package/
        requirements:
          run:
            - cmake >=3.20
            - ninja
        script:
          - if: unix
            then: cmake -S find-package -B find-package-build -G Ninja -DEXPECT_TOOL=ON -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="${CONDA_PREFIX}"
            else: cmake -S find-package -B find-package-build -G Ninja -DEXPECT_TOOL=ON -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="%CONDA_PREFIX%\Library"
    about:
      summary: libclang/libtooling C++ introspection - pybind11 bindings, .pyi stubs, Sphinx docs, JSON IR
      description: |
        Apiary is a standalone libclang/libtooling tool that, from a single AST
        walk over annotated C++ headers, emits pybind11 (or nanobind) bindings,
        .pyi type stubs, Sphinx C++ API documentation (including macros, no
        Doxygen), and a structured public-API JSON IR.

        It ships an installable CMake package: find_package(Apiary COMPONENTS tool)
        provides the apiary::apiary executable, the apiary::annotations INTERFACE
        header target (the APIARY_* annotation macros, from apiary-annotations),
        and the apiary_* helper functions that wire codegen into a downstream build.

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/Einsums/Apiary
  summary: libclang/libtooling C++ introspection - pybind11 bindings, .pyi stubs, Sphinx docs, JSON IR
  license: MIT
  license_file: LICENSE.txt
  documentation: https://einsums.github.io/Apiary/
  repository: https://github.com/Einsums/Apiary

extra:
  feedstock-name: apiary
  recipe-maintainers:
    - jturney
